tutorials.intro: Step-by-step guides to help you get started with network testing.

cir.techDef: The guaranteed bandwidth as specified in a service level agreement, below which the network commits to deliver traffic with minimal loss or delay.
cir.laymanDef: The speed your internet/network contract guarantees you will always get.

eir.techDef: The rate above CIR up to which the network will attempt to deliver frames, but without guarantees.
eir.laymanDef: Bonus bandwidth you might get when the network is not busy, but no promises.

bandwidth.techDef: Maximum rate of data transfer across a network path, typically measured in bits per second.
bandwidth.laymanDef: How much data can flow through your connection per second - like water through a pipe.

throughput.techDef: The actual rate of successful data transfer, accounting for protocol overhead and network conditions.
throughput.laymanDef: How much useful data actually gets through - slightly less than bandwidth due to overhead.

latency.techDef: The time delay for a packet to travel from source to destination.
latency.laymanDef: The "lag" - how long it takes for your data to reach the other end.

rtt.techDef: The time for a signal to travel to a destination and back, including processing delays.
rtt.laymanDef: How long a round trip takes - send a message, get a reply.

jitter.techDef: The variation in latency between successive packets in a flow.
jitter.laymanDef: How much the delay wobbles around - matters for video calls and gaming.

pdv.techDef: ITU-T standard term for jitter, measuring the difference in delay between packets.
pdv.laymanDef: The technical name for jitter - timing inconsistency.

pps.techDef: The rate at which network packets are processed or transmitted.
pps.laymanDef: How many packets your network can handle each second.

mpps.techDef: Standard unit for measuring high-speed packet processing rates.
mpps.laymanDef: Millions of packets per second - for measuring fast switches and routers.

mtu.techDef: The largest packet size (in bytes) that can be transmitted without fragmentation.
mtu.laymanDef: The biggest chunk of data you can send at once - usually 1500 bytes.

jumbo_frames.techDef: Ethernet frames larger than 1500 bytes, typically up to 9000 bytes.
jumbo_frames.laymanDef: Extra-large packets for data centers - more efficient but need special support.

mac.techDef: Layer 2 hardware address that uniquely identifies network interfaces.
mac.laymanDef: The address used to identify an interface on an Ethernet network; it may be configured or randomized.

dut.techDef: The network device being tested and evaluated.

sut.techDef: The complete system including all devices in the test path.
sut.laymanDef: Everything you are testing together as a system.

sla.techDef: Contractual agreement specifying performance guarantees and penalties.
sla.laymanDef: The contract that says what your provider promises to deliver.

oam.techDef: Tools and protocols for monitoring and managing networks, including Y.1731.
oam.laymanDef: Built-in network monitoring tools that carriers use.

cfm.techDef: IEEE 802.1ag protocol for detecting and isolating connectivity faults.
cfm.laymanDef: System for automatically finding network problems.

xdp.techDef: Linux kernel technology for high-performance packet processing before the network stack.
xdp.laymanDef: Fast-path technology that processes packets super quickly.

afxdp.techDef: Linux socket type for zero-copy packet processing using XDP.
afxdp.laymanDef: Way to handle network packets extremely fast in Linux.

tos.techDef: IPv4 header field used for quality of service prioritization.
tos.laymanDef: Tag in IP packets to mark priority level.

dscp.techDef: 6-bit field in IP header for traffic classification and QoS.
dscp.laymanDef: Modern way to mark packet priority - tells the network how important a packet is.

cos.techDef: 3-bit field in VLAN tag for Layer 2 traffic classification (IEEE 802.1p).
cos.laymanDef: Priority marking at the Ethernet level (layer 2).

vlan.techDef: Logical network partition at Layer 2, typically using IEEE 802.1Q tagging.
vlan.laymanDef: Virtual networks that keep traffic separated on the same physical equipment.

qinq.techDef: Stacking of VLAN tags for provider/customer separation.
qinq.laymanDef: Putting a VLAN tag inside another VLAN tag - used by carriers.

bdp.techDef: Product of bandwidth and RTT, representing data in flight for optimal TCP.
bdp.laymanDef: How much data should be "in the air" at once for maximum speed.

tcp.techDef: Connection-oriented transport protocol with reliability and flow control.
tcp.laymanDef: The protocol that makes sure data arrives correctly and in order.

udp.techDef: Connectionless transport protocol without reliability guarantees.
udp.laymanDef: Fast but unreliable - used for video streaming and gaming.

tsn.techDef: IEEE 802.1 standards for deterministic, low-latency Ethernet communication.
tsn.laymanDef: Ethernet features that control transmission timing and bound delay when correctly configured.

tas.techDef: IEEE 802.1Qbv mechanism for scheduled traffic transmission.
tas.laymanDef: Network feature that opens and closes time gates for traffic.

gcl.techDef: Schedule defining when traffic classes can transmit in TSN.
gcl.laymanDef: The schedule that says when each type of traffic can go.

reflector.techDef: Endpoint that returns received packets for round-trip measurement.
reflector.laymanDef: Device at the far end that bounces packets back for testing.

loopback.techDef: Interface or mechanism that returns traffic to its source.
loopback.laymanDef: Sending traffic back to where it came from for testing.

binary_search.techDef: Algorithm that halves the search space each iteration to find optimal rate.
binary_search.laymanDef: Quickly finding the right speed by trying half as much each time.

frame_loss.techDef: Percentage of transmitted frames that fail to arrive at destination.
frame_loss.laymanDef: Packets that got lost along the way.

benchmark.techDef: Evaluate equipment throughput, latency, loss and burst handling on an isolated test network.
benchmark.laymanDef: Evaluate equipment throughput, latency, loss and burst handling on an isolated test network.

servicetest.techDef: Check service configuration and sustained performance against the agreed acceptance criteria.
servicetest.laymanDef: Check service configuration and sustained performance against the agreed acceptance criteria.

trafficgen.techDef: Generate a defined traffic pattern with the selected rate, frame size and duration.
trafficgen.laymanDef: Generate a defined traffic pattern with the selected rate, frame size and duration.

measure.techDef: Use Y.1731 OAM measurements to check service delay, loss and connectivity.
measure.laymanDef: Use Y.1731 OAM measurements to check service delay, loss and connectivity.

certify.techDef: Run switch, TCP and TSN tests against configured thresholds. The module name does not imply third-party certification.
certify.laymanDef: Run switch, TCP and TSN tests against configured thresholds. The module name does not imply third-party certification.

history.techDef: Review completed runs and their measurements. Select a run to inspect its result or remove an unneeded entry.
history.laymanDef: Review completed runs and their measurements. Select a run to inspect its result or remove an unneeded entry.

security.techDef: Manage multi-factor authentication and security keys for the signed-in account. Keep recovery codes available before changing access methods.
security.laymanDef: Manage multi-factor authentication and security keys for the signed-in account. Keep recovery codes available before changing access methods.

detail.copyCommand: Copy this command to the clipboard so you can paste it in a terminal

advanced.bidirectionalHelp: Run tests in both directions simultaneously.

duration.perTestHelp: Duration for each test iteration. Longer durations provide more accurate results but take more time.
duration.trialsHelp: Number of times to repeat each test point. More trials improve statistical accuracy.
duration.warmupHelp: Time to stabilize traffic flow before starting measurements.

frameLoss.stepSizeHelp: Load increment step for frame loss rate measurement.

frameSizes.help: Select frame sizes to test. RFC 2544 specifies: 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 1280, 1518 bytes.

throughput.maxLossHelp: Maximum frame loss considered acceptable. RFC 2544 specifies 0%.

params.durationHelp: Duration for each test iteration in seconds.

switch.addressCountHelp: Number of MAC addresses for learning/caching tests. RFC 2889 recommends testing at 1, 10, 100, 1000, 10000 addresses.
switch.lossHelp: Maximum acceptable frame loss percentage. RFC 2889 specifies 0%.
switch.patternHelp: How traffic is distributed across ports.
switch.portCountHelp: Number of switch ports to test.

network.targetRateHelp: Target throughput rate for TCP testing.

tcp.rwndHelp: TCP Receive Window size. Should be >= BDP for optimal throughput.

burst.enableTitle: Send frames in short bursts separated by idle gaps rather than at a continuous rate; useful for testing buffer behavior

mac.dstHelp: Destination MAC address (leave empty for broadcast). Format: AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF.
mac.srcHelp: Source MAC address (leave empty for auto). Format: AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF.

stream.idHelp: Unique identifier for this traffic stream.

traffic.rateHelp: Traffic rate as percentage of interface line rate.

ptp.enableTitle: Use IEEE 1588 PTP hardware timestamps for sub-microsecond delay measurement; requires PTP-capable NIC
ptp.requireTitle: Block the test from starting until the local PTP clock has locked to the grandmaster within the configured tolerance

scheduling.baseTimeHelp: Base time for gate schedule (ns since epoch). 0 = use current time.
scheduling.preemptionTitle: Allow express traffic to preempt in-flight preemptable frames per IEEE 802.1Qbu; reduces latency for critical traffic classes

timing.maxLatencyHelp: Maximum acceptable end-to-end latency in nanoseconds.

bandwidth.cbsHelp: Committed Burst Size - maximum burst of traffic allowed at CIR before excess marking.
bandwidth.cirHelp: Committed Information Rate - the guaranteed bandwidth that the service will always provide.
bandwidth.ebsHelp: Excess Burst Size - maximum burst of excess traffic (beyond CIR) that may be allowed.
bandwidth.eirHelp: Excess Information Rate - additional bandwidth available when network capacity permits (best-effort).

duration.configStepHelp: Duration for each step load (25%, 50%, 75%, 100% of CIR) during configuration test.
duration.perfHelp: Duration of the sustained performance test at 100% CIR. Y.1564 recommends minimum 15 minutes (900s).

frameSizes.help: Select frame sizes to test. RFC 2544 recommends: 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 1280, 1518 bytes.

sla.fdHelp: Maximum acceptable one-way Frame Delay (FD). Typical values: 5-50ms depending on service class.
sla.fdvHelp: Maximum acceptable Frame Delay Variation (FDV/jitter). Typical values: 2-10ms.
sla.flrHelp: Maximum acceptable Frame Loss Ratio (FLR). Typical SLA values: 0.01% to 0.1%.

vlan.colorAwareHelp: Enable dual-rate testing with green (CIR) and yellow (EIR) traffic classes.
vlan.idHelp: VLAN tag for test traffic. Set to 0 for untagged traffic.

measurement.countHelp: Number of measurement frames per interval.

mep.megLevelHelp: Maintenance Entity Group level (0-7). Higher = wider domain.

oam.ccmHelp: Continuity Check Message interval per Y.1731.
oam.taggedTitle: Add an IEEE 802.1Q VLAN tag with the selected priority to all Y.1731 OAM frames

tooltips.showPassword: Show the password to verify what you typed
